evidence_scope_projection.definition: Overall prostate cancer evidence, excluding estimates solely about aggressive prostate cancer. General estimates from papers that also report aggressive endpoints remain included. Uncertain endpoints retain their existing review and pooling restrictions.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an effect size of 0.68 (95% CI: 0.38–1.23), indicating no statistically significant association between insoluble dietary fiber intake and prostate cancer\aggressive. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 80.73%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.

disease_scope_original_row.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: this study examined the relationship between fiber intake and the risk of PCa

cases.excerpt: Therefore, this study examined the relationship between fiber intake and the risk of PCa by using data from Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial. A total of 54,336 participants in the United States, consisting of 6,414 patients with PCa, were included in this study.

comparison.excerpt: Compared with individuals in the lowest quartile, individuals in the highest quartile of insoluble fiber intake

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared with individuals in the lowest quartile, individuals in the highest quartile of insoluble fiber intake had a significantly lower risk of PCa (aHR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.78-0.98).

continent.excerpt: A total of 54,336 participants in the United States, consisting of 6,414 patients with PCa, were included in this study.

effect_size.excerpt: Compared with individuals in the lowest quartile, individuals in the highest quartile of insoluble fiber intake had a significantly lower risk of PCa (aHR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.78-0.98). By contrast, no significant associations were detected between total fiber intake (aHR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.80-1.01) or soluble fiber intake (aHR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.80-1.02).

exposure_measurement.excerpt: this study examined the relationship between fiber intake and the risk of PCa

p_value.excerpt: As shown in Table 2 , compared with those of subjects in the lowest quartile of insoluble fiber (Q1), the aHRs of PCa risk were 0.97 (95% CI, 0.90–1.05; P = 0.453), 0.97 (95% CI, 0.90–1.06; P = 0.526), and 0.87 (95% CI, 0.78–0.98; P = 0.016) for groups Q2, Q3, and Q4, respectively.
p_value.location: Results, “Associations between fiber intake and PCa risk,” paragraph 1

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 54,336 participants in the United States, consisting of 6,414 patients with PCa, were included in this study.

timing.excerpt: The median follow-up times for the PCa and control groups were 5.9 years and 11.5 years, respectively.
